opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Black (employee ID E008) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E008.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Black (E008) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. She requested admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted. As a full-time employee, maximum is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E008 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; admin is never allowed. Karen requested admin to Source Code, but her max is read. HR note claimed full-time, but Security DB record shows contractor. Recommend read.
reason: Karen Black (E008) requested admin to Source Code. Security DB shows she is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training, and admin is never permitted. Since admin exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum allowed level: read. The Security agent's note (authoritative DB record) conflicts with HR's note; following the Security record, the maximum is read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Karen Black (E008), requesting admin access to Source Code.

Two notes conflict:
- HR note: full_time Payroll Specialist, recommendation write
- Security note: contractor with basic security training, recommendation read

The notes conflict on employment status. HR says full-time, Security says contractor. Security DB shows contractor. The Security agent's recommendation is read (contractor with basic training → max read).

Per policy:
- If full_time: max write (admin only if role owns system; Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code, Engineer does). So max write.
- If contractor with basic training: read (write only if advanced training). So max read.

The request is admin, which is above both maximums. So grant the maximum.

Which employment type to trust? The Security DB record shows contractor. The Security agent's note is the most recent relevant check on actual access privileges. Typically in these scenarios, Security is authoritative for access levels. The recommendation from Security is read.

Given conflict, I should probably follow the Security note (contractor, basic training) → max read. Grant read.

Actually, let me think. The team memory has two notes. The Approver makes final decision. The Security agent has access to Security DB which is the authoritative record for employment/access. HR may have outdated info. Recommend read.

Submit decision: read.
